rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i2441 p. 4, earned income (line 1z, here without line 1e, plus net self-employment earnings). The candidate copies its person.dc_earned (box 1 plus line 3 less line 13), which without line 1e is exactly lines 18/19 earned income; no value differs. The at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return") is a cited scope refusal. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the Schedule SE conditions the screen lists that can arise without one (church employee income, clergy income, partnership self-employment income, farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (the project refuses it at person.credit through Schedule 3 line 11 on every return). The candidate refusals (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8959.1, classm.s179.1, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen supplied true and no Schedule C; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. In the deepseek-flash candidate graph every return with a Schedule C is unevaluable: its person.income179 reads person.sc_total, which reads sc.line31, which reads the section 179 deduction limited by s179.income, which reads person.income179 ("cycle at person[...].sc_total"; classm.asset.1, classm.asset.3, classm.f8889.2.deepseek). That cycle is ruled a model error at person.income179; here it only masks evaluation. The candidate also reaches s179.mfs on married-filing-separately returns (classm.f8959.2, classm.scveh.2, gen#71), which the project refuses for every married filing separately return at scope.ready (s3.mfs), and the project's s179.multi refusals (classm.s179.2, gen#94; i4562 p. 5, Line 12) are cited scope refusals. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/person.deepseek.json): 2,335 of 4,647 comparisons agree; 220 candidate-refuses, 2085 candidate-unknown, 7 project-refuses.

By reading it is Schedule C less Schedule SE line 13 on every return, which equals EIC Worksheet B Part 1 or Part 2 wherever line 13 is zero without Schedule SE.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040gi EIC Worksheet B, Part 1 and Part 2 (Schedule SE line 3 less line 13 if you file Schedule SE, otherwise Schedule C line 31), with i1040sse p. 1, Who Must File Schedule SE: "You must file Schedule SE if: The amount on line 4c of Schedule SE is $400 or more, or You had church employee income of $108.28 or more." The candidate always takes line 3 less line 13; below the $400 threshold line 13 is zero and line 3 is the Schedule C total, so the value equals the project's choice. The at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return") is a cited scope refusal. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the Schedule SE conditions the screen lists that can arise without one (church employee income, clergy income, partnership self-employment income, farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (the project refuses it at person.credit through Schedule 3 line 11 on every return). The candidate refusals (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8959.1, classm.s179.1, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen supplied true and no Schedule C; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. In the deepseek-flash candidate graph every return with a Schedule C is unevaluable: its person.income179 reads person.sc_total, which reads sc.line31, which reads the section 179 deduction limited by s179.income, which reads person.income179 ("cycle at person[...].sc_total"; classm.asset.1, classm.asset.3, classm.f8889.2.deepseek). That cycle is ruled a model error at person.income179; here it only masks evaluation. The candidate also reaches s179.mfs on married-filing-separately returns (classm.f8959.2, classm.scveh.2, gen#71), which the project refuses for every married filing separately return at scope.ready (s3.mfs), and the project's s179.multi refusals (classm.s179.2, gen#94; i4562 p. 5, Line 12) are cited scope refusals. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/person.deepseek.json): 2,317 of 4,647 comparisons agree; 220 candidate-refuses, 2103 candidate-unknown, 7 project-refuses.

Not executable: the reply fails validation (person.h_se_line4a_mult: "declared NonNegDollars but the expression does not prove non-negativity"), so triage cannot run any of its lines (triage/person.deepseek.json, state invalid); this line's candidate reaches person.h_se_line4a_mult (92.35% of its Schedule SE line 3, which is Schedule C line 31 and can be a loss; its guard uses the product only when line 3 is above zero, but the declared type is not proved) through Schedule 1 lines 15 and 16 in its line 4 (s1.line15 and s1.line16 sum its person.se_line13 and person.s16), so no value of it was computed. By reading: i1040gi p. 97, line 4: "Enter the total of the amounts from Schedule 1, lines 11 through 19a, plus 23 and 25"; line 5: "Subtract line 4 from line 3". The reply recomputes lines 3 to 5 per person from f1040.line9 less Schedule 1 lines 11, 13, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19a, 24a and 25: it subtracts line 24a (jury duty pay), which line 4 does not list, and omits 23 (lines 12, 14 and 23 are screened by scope.schedule1 ("an adjustment on Schedule 1 line 12, 14 or 23"), so they are zero), so with jury duty pay its modified AGI is too low and line 6 too high.

The candidate subtracts Form 1040 line 11a, adjusted gross income after the IRA deduction itself, from line 2: a different and circular base (line 11a reads Schedule 1 line 20, which reads this worksheet). For a single covered filer with $80,000 of wages and a $7,000 contribution the worksheet gives line 6 $9,000 ($89,000 less $80,000); the candidate figures it from AGI after the deduction (derived from the expressions, not executed).

The reply's Schedule SE has no $400 test (se.floor was published): it figures 92.35% of Schedule C line 31 and the tax on it for any positive amount, so a person with $300 of net profit owes self-employment tax ($300 x 0.9235 x 15.3% = $42.39 by its expression) where the source says stop. It also drops the Schedule C gate (person.has_sc) and reads sc.line31 for sc.result (the cited at-risk refusal, scope). Lines 8 to 10 (the social security wage base less person.wages, boxes 3 and 7, amb.2025.ss_wages) and the 2.9% part are the source's.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040sse p. 1, Who Must File Schedule SE: "You must file Schedule SE if: The amount on line 4c of Schedule SE is $400 or more, or You had church employee income of $108.28 or more." The project (sc.result inside person.se_line2, has_sc gate) and the candidate (sum of sc.line31) give the same line; sc.result equals sc.line31 except that a loss with some investment not at risk is refused at sc.loss_allowed (i1040sc p. The at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return") is a cited scope refusal. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the Schedule SE conditions the screen lists that can arise without one (church employee income, clergy income, partnership self-employment income, farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (the project refuses it at person.credit through Schedule 3 line 11 on every return). The candidate refusals (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8959.1, classm.s179.1, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen supplied true and no Schedule C; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. The deepseek-flash line rebuilds Schedule SE from helpers (line 4c, line 10 on the smaller of line 6 or the wage base less wages, line 11, half of line 12) and agrees with the project's se definition wherever both evaluate. In the deepseek-flash candidate graph every return with a Schedule C is unevaluable: its person.income179 reads person.sc_total, which reads sc.line31, which reads the section 179 deduction limited by s179.income, which reads person.income179 ("cycle at person[...].sc_total"; classm.asset.1, classm.asset.3, classm.f8889.2.deepseek). That cycle is ruled a model error at person.income179; here it only masks evaluation. The candidate also reaches s179.mfs on married-filing-separately returns (classm.f8959.2, classm.scveh.2, gen#71), which the project refuses for every married filing separately return at scope.ready (s3.mfs), and the project's s179.multi refusals (classm.s179.2, gen#94; i4562 p. 5, Line 12) are cited scope refusals. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/person.deepseek.json): 2,317 of 4,647 comparisons agree; 220 candidate-refuses, 2103 candidate-unknown, 7 project-refuses.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040sse p. 1, Who Must File Schedule SE: "You must file Schedule SE if: The amount on line 4c of Schedule SE is $400 or more, or You had church employee income of $108.28 or more." The project (sc.result inside person.se_line2, has_sc gate) and the candidate (sum of sc.line31) give the same line; sc.result equals sc.line31 except that a loss with some investment not at risk is refused at sc.loss_allowed (i1040sc p. The at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return") is a cited scope refusal. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the Schedule SE conditions the screen lists that can arise without one (church employee income, clergy income, partnership self-employment income, farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (the project refuses it at person.credit through Schedule 3 line 11 on every return). The candidate refusals (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8959.1, classm.s179.1, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen supplied true and no Schedule C; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. The deepseek-flash line rebuilds Schedule SE from helpers (line 4c, line 10 on the smaller of line 6 or the wage base less wages, line 11, half of line 12) and agrees with the project's se definition wherever both evaluate. In the deepseek-flash candidate graph every return with a Schedule C is unevaluable: its person.income179 reads person.sc_total, which reads sc.line31, which reads the section 179 deduction limited by s179.income, which reads person.income179 ("cycle at person[...].sc_total"; classm.asset.1, classm.asset.3, classm.f8889.2.deepseek). That cycle is ruled a model error at person.income179; here it only masks evaluation. The candidate also reaches s179.mfs on married-filing-separately returns (classm.f8959.2, classm.scveh.2, gen#71), which the project refuses for every married filing separately return at scope.ready (s3.mfs), and the project's s179.multi refusals (classm.s179.2, gen#94; i4562 p. 5, Line 12) are cited scope refusals. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/person.deepseek.json): 2,317 of 4,647 comparisons agree; 220 candidate-refuses, 2103 candidate-unknown, 7 project-refuses.
